questions.questionText: What fundamentally turns a plain LLM call into an "agent"?
options: Using a larger or more expensive model
Giving the model tools it can call plus a loop that lets it act, observe the result, and decide what to do next
Fine-tuning the model on more data
Running the model on a GPU instead of a CPU
questions.correctAnswer: Giving the model tools it can call plus a loop that lets it act, observe the result, and decide what to do next
questions.explanation: The model itself doesn't change — what makes it an agent is the scaffolding: tools it can invoke and a control loop that lets it act and react to results before answering.

questions.questionText: Why can't a plain, tool-less LLM reliably answer "What's the weather in Tokyo right now?"
options: LLMs cannot process questions about weather
Its knowledge is frozen at training time and it has no way to check live, current information
Weather questions require a different type of neural network
It's a trick question with no correct answer
questions.correctAnswer: Its knowledge is frozen at training time and it has no way to check live, current information
questions.explanation: Without a tool to check current data, the model can only draw on what it learned during training — which has no way of reflecting real-time conditions.

questions.questionText: What are the three core ingredients every agent is built from?
options: A database, a frontend, and an API
A model, tools it can call, and a control loop that executes those calls and feeds results back in
A GPU, a dataset, and a loss function
A prompt, a temperature setting, and a max token limit
questions.correctAnswer: A model, tools it can call, and a control loop that executes those calls and feeds results back in
questions.explanation: Every agent framework, regardless of implementation details, is built from these three pieces working together.
